events_chronological: Elliot Farb grows up in a house under a seaside amusement pier, depressed at nine because the universe is expanding.
At school Elliot kisses a girl in class, and his classmates stand up one by one to announce what they grew up to be.
Elliot does his army service entertaining troops and becomes a stand-up comedian in the city.
Elliot's first marriage, to Judith, fails while he obsesses over a political assassination in bed.
Elliot's second marriage, to Carol, fails amid literary parties and her refusal to be interrupted.
Elliot meets Peggy Rowan after a tennis game with his friend Max, and she drives him home terrifyingly and asks him up for wine.
Elliot and Peggy's first date ends in bed, and afterwards she needs a cigarette.
Peggy moves in with Elliot, who pushes her into adult-education classes and books about death.
Elliot sends Peggy to an analyst and pays for it, and their two sessions are played side by side in split screen.
Elliot and Peggy visit her family in a farm town, where her grandmother stares at him and he sees himself at the table as a figure from another century.
Peggy's brother Neil confides his urge to steer into oncoming headlights, and then drives them to the airport.
Elliot and Peggy break up, and each of them tries seeing other people.
Peggy calls Elliot at three in the morning about a spider in the bathroom, and they get back together.
Peggy starts singing in clubs and is courted professionally by the record producer Sy Kale.
Elliot and Peggy fly to the coast for a television award, and Elliot hates every minute of it.
On the flight back each of them concedes, in unspoken narration, that it has ended.
Elliot flies back to the coast to propose, is turned down in a health-food restaurant, and crashes a rental car.
Elliot writes a play in which the woman says yes, and admits to the audience that you can do that in art.
Elliot and Peggy meet again in the city as friends, and he watches her walk away.
Elliot tells the joke about the man whose brother thinks he is a chicken, and says relationships are irrational but we keep going through them anyway.
nonlinear_category_reason: The affair is the spine and runs forward, while childhood, the army and two earlier marriages drop in from before it as the comedian free-associates.
syuzhet_notes: The comedian narrates straight to camera and moves by association rather than by clock, so the film announces the break-up at told-order bullet 5 before showing the meeting at bullet 6, and drops his two earlier marriages in at bullets 8-9, well after the affair they precede. Told-order bullets 2-4 are childhood and early-career flashbacks, and he repeatedly walks into his own past scenes as an adult to argue with the people in them.
fabula_notes: The film gives no dates, so the ordering of the two marriages relative to each other and to the main affair is inferred from the narration. The play at told-order bullet 19 is a fiction written about events already shown, not a further event in the relationship.

events.content: A boy of nine under a seaside pier explains to a doctor that the universe is expanding and will one day come apart, so there is no point in finishing anything.
events.location: a house under an amusement pier

events.content: Doubles at an indoor court, a terrible drive home in which she uses the whole road, and a glass of wine on a terrace where neither of them says a single sentence that means what it says.

events.content: In the play the restaurant is the same and the man says the same words, and this time the woman says yes and comes back with him, and he turns to the audience and admits what he has just done.

reader: the film's thesis about art, stated by a character who is in one

events.content: Two people outside a cinema in the afternoon, catching up pleasantly, and then one of them crosses the road and the camera stays where it is.

events.content: A man's brother thinks he is a chicken. Asked why he does not turn him in, the man says he needs the eggs. That, he says, is more or less how he feels about relationships.
